group.passage: For more than 80 years, a bear in a ranger's hat has been reminding Americans to be careful with fire. Smokey Bear is the face of the longest public service campaign the United States has ever run. Yet the message he delivers has not stayed exactly the same. The campaign was born during World War II. In 1942, a Japanese submarine fired shells at an oil field on the California coast, close to a national forest. Officials feared that enemy attacks could set the western forests ablaze, and since many firefighters had been sent overseas, preventing fires became a national priority. Because nine out of ten forest fires were started by people, careless behavior was the obvious target. A poster borrowing a deer from a Disney film proved popular, but the studio had lent the character for a single year. Needing an animal of its own, the Forest Service picked a bear in 1944. Smokey soon became a national celebrity. His famous slogan, "Only you can prevent forest fires," first appeared in 1947. Three years later, firefighters in New Mexico found a real bear cub clinging to a burned tree, his paws and legs badly injured. After treatment, the cub was sent to the National Zoo in Washington, D.C., where he became the living Smokey Bear and received so much mail that he was given his own postal code. For five decades, his message suggested that every fire in the woods was an enemy to be defeated. Over time, however, experts began to question this view. Many landscapes had in fact been shaped by fire, and Native peoples had long used it to care for the land. After decades in which nearly every fire was put out, dead wood and thick plant growth piled up, leaving many areas even more likely to burn. In 2001, the slogan became "Only you can prevent wildfires." A wildfire is any unwanted fire burning outdoors, whether in a forest or on grassland. The new wording separates such dangerous fires from planned burns that experts carry out to keep the land healthy. Smokey still has plenty of work to do, though: people cause about 80 percent of the wildfires in the country.

translation_zh.text:
森林防火熊的演變

八十多年來，一隻戴著巡山員帽子的熊一直提醒美國人小心用火。「Smokey Bear」是美國有史以來持續最久的公益宣傳活動的代言角色。然而，他傳達的訊息並非一成不變。

這個活動誕生於第二次世界大戰期間。1942 年，一艘日本潛艇向加州海岸一處靠近國家森林的油田發射砲彈。官員擔心敵人的攻擊可能讓西部的森林陷入火海，而且由於許多消防員已被派往海外，防止火災成了國家的優先要務。由於每十場森林火災就有九場是人引起的，粗心的行為自然成為宣導的目標。一張借用迪士尼電影中小鹿的海報大受歡迎，但片廠只把這個角色借出一年。由於需要一個屬於自己的動物，林務局在 1944 年選中了一隻熊。

Smokey 很快成為全國知名的明星。他著名的口號「只有你能防止森林火災」在 1947 年首度出現。三年後，新墨西哥州的消防員發現一隻真實的小熊緊抱著一棵燒焦的樹，腳掌和腿都嚴重受傷。治療之後，這隻小熊被送到華盛頓特區的國家動物園，成了「活的 Smokey Bear」，而且收到的信多到他被給予專屬的郵遞區號。五十年來，他的訊息暗示森林裡的每一場火都是必須打敗的敵人。

然而，隨著時間過去，專家開始質疑這個看法。許多地景其實是由火塑造出來的，而原住民長久以來都用火來照顧土地。在幾乎每一場火都被撲滅的數十年之後，枯木和茂密的植物越積越多，反而讓許多地區更容易燃燒。

2001 年，口號改成「只有你能防止野火」。野火指的是任何在戶外燃燒、不受歡迎的火，不論是在森林裡還是草原上。新的用字把這類危險的火，和專家為了讓土地保持健康而有計畫地進行的燃燒區分開來。不過，Smokey 仍有很多工作要做：這個國家約有百分之八十的野火是人引起的。
